# @netlify/redirect-matcher

Netlify's redirect rule matcher, compiled to WebAssembly, for matching requests
against Netlify redirect rules in local tooling.

```js
import { createMatcher } from '@netlify/redirect-matcher'

const matcher = await createMatcher(rules, { jwtSecret, jwtRoleClaim })
const result = matcher.match({ scheme: 'https', host, path, query, headers, cookies })

if (result?.type === 'match') {
  console.log(result.status, result.to)
}

matcher.close()
```

`rules` is the JSON produced by `@netlify/redirect-parser`, as a string or an
array. Rules that fail to parse are skipped and listed in
`matcher.parseErrors`. `match` returns `null` when nothing matched, and
`{ type: 'forcedNotFound' }` when a role-gated rule rejected the request and no
later rule matched.

`headers` and `cookies` may be plain objects or iterables of `[name, value]`
pairs, such as `Headers` or `Map`. Header names are matched case-insensitively,
so names that differ only in case collide, and the last one wins. A header
whose value is an array matches on its first element, and `null` or
`undefined` values are treated as absent.

Loading the matcher defines these globals, which Go's WebAssembly runtime
needs: `globalThis.Go`, `globalThis.__netlifyRedirectMatcher`, and, if they
are not already defined, stub `globalThis.fs` and `globalThis.path` objects.

Requires Node.js 22.12 or later.
